text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000088 bills 99215 well above expectation at every complexity level, including patients with few chronic conditions, but the small set of returned charts supports the billed levels, so the evidence is mixed.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The 99215 excess is not confined to sicker patients. The by-complexity table shows elevated shares even for patients with 0 or 1 conditions. Sampled low-complexity 99215s carry routine diagnoses such as urinary tract infection (C0047837, C0048213), upper respiratory infection (C0048004, C0048271) or follow-up only (C0048018, C0048291), which is a pattern consistent with upcoding rather than a high-acuity panel. Against that, the documented 99215 claims all support high MDM (e.g., C0048101, C0048189), and there is no sign of cloned data-review notes. However, only 6 documented 99215 claims is too thin to settle the question, especially since most 99215s fall on low-complexity patients. The 99214 unsupported rate is above the all-provider rate (C0048020, C0048143), but it rests on 2 claims and is only a weak signal. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, such as C0048045, C0048224 and C0048279, to test whether documentation supports high MDM on simple acute or follow-up visits."}
